label: thm:geometry-of-incompleteness
title: The geometry of incompleteness: a Turing-complete QOU has a nonempty horizon
html:
Given a QOU whose substrate is Turing-complete, the jet horizon \mathcal{H} = V(\mathfrak{h}) is non-empty: there exists a degree-0 datum whose truth is inaccessible. Equivalently, the degree-0 sections vanish on a non-trivial region, \Gamma(\mathcal{H}, A_0) = 0.

A degree-0 datum is an observable answer read off the substrate — a decision result, a particle identity, or the truth value of a self-referential sentence. It is inaccessible — behind the horizon — when it fails either route to access:

  • formally, it is unprovable (Gödel incompleteness, forced in any substrate expressive enough to encode arithmetic — every q \neq 1 substrate, whose q-Toffoli gates are universal); or
  • physically, extracting it is super-polynomial. For the boundary family a bandwidth-limited device must read the full 3^{3n}-leaf surviving skein resolution tree, so by the Bekenstein bandwidth bound its step count grows faster than every polynomial (the physical-intractability theorem).

These are two witnesses of one phenomenon — the vanishing of degree-0 sections. Gödel supplies a formally-inaccessible degree-0 datum; the resolution-tree information bound supplies a physically-intractable one. Either establishes a non-empty horizon; the QOU exhibits both, so the horizon is doubly confirmed. In the framework's reading, this common cause is exactly what a black-hole event horizon is: the region across which degree-0 truth cannot pass while degree-\geq 1 data (witnesses, Hawking radiation) leaks. The event horizon is the geometry of incompleteness.

Scope (what this does and does not say). This is an existence / necessity statement about the substrate's structure — a Turing-complete QOU must host an inaccessible degree-0 region. It is not a proof of \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP}. The step from "the observation trace is intractable to extract" to "\mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP}" is a counting-to-decision transfer that no known result supplies and that a generic argument cannot (a \#\mathrm{P}-hard count can sit atop a poly-time decision, as for perfect matchings). The physical-intractability leg is genuinely derived; the formal-incompleteness leg is Gödel's theorem; only the identification of this joint inaccessibility with the black-hole horizon is the framework's degree-0 interpretation.
